solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: World Cup-winning footballer fades

definitions.meaning: Martin ... scored for England in their 1966 World Cup final win
to peter out is to dwindle away, so it fades

explanation.definitionFit: A surname of a 1966 England winner doubles as the verb meaning dwindles, as in a stream that peters out.

clue.text: Having this, belt's tight in fat person — not half

definitions.text: Having this, belt's tight in fat person — not half

indicators.note: in puts the jumbled belt inside the shortened fat person
not half drops the first half of the rhyming word for a plump person

parts.note: a roly-poly is a fat person

indicators.note: tight in its sense of drunk signals the letters are disordered

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Someone with a paunch finds their belt tight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' here means drunk, so it signals the anagram; 'not half' drops the first half of the fat person. Read as a whole, the clue also describes having a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot belly, a protruding stomach, would make a belt feel tight on a fat person.

clue.text: Spare toothless so-and-so

parts.note: spare means lean or thin
gummy means showing gums and no teeth

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at some skinny, toothless individual.
explanation.definitionFit: Thingummy is a placeholder name for something or someone you can't name, just like so-and-so.

clue.text: More embarrassed about English member of stag party?

indicators.note: about puts the word for more embarrassed around the abbreviation

parts.note: redder means blushing more

explanation.surface: An English groom-to-be blushes more on his stag do.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag party sounds like a groom's night out, but here it is a herd of deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A red deer is a species whose males are stags, so one belongs to a group of stags.

clue.text: Fine porcelain gives cheer to unpleasant place

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge or cheer them, so 'eggs' gives cheer to
hell is the proverbial unpleasant place

explanation.surface: Some delicate china seems to be cheering up a grim spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggshell porcelain is an extremely thin, translucent kind of fine china.

clue.text: Suitable position at university for convivial company

parts.note: good means suitable or fit
a fellowship is a research or teaching post at a university

explanation.surface: An appropriate academic post goes with sociable colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: Good fellowship is friendly, sociable companionship, the same idea as convivial company.

clue.text: Group of musicians met an artful composer

indicators.note: Group of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A band encounters a crafty songwriter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedřich Smetana was the Czech composer of Má vlast and The Bartered Bride.

clue.text: Top people from European Commission in English language teaching

indicators.note: in puts the commission's initials inside those of the teaching

parts.note: ELT is the standard abbreviation for English language teaching

explanation.surface: Senior figures from the European Commission get involved in teaching English.
explanation.definitionFit: The elect are a chosen elite, the select few at the top.

clue.text: Reprieves pullets heartlessly getting the chop

indicators.note: getting the chop suggests being chopped up, so the remaining letters are rearranged
heartlessly takes out the central letter of the poultry word

explanation.surface: Young hens are callously slaughtered with no reprieve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' removes the middle L of PULLETS, and 'getting the chop' rearranges PULETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Let-ups are pauses or easings, breaks that give relief like a reprieve.

clue.text: Comparison in adverts making crazy offer and rebate

indicators.note: crazy says the letters of the following phrase go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Advertisements make a mad offer of a discount.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'and' is part of the anagram fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Before-and-after pictures are the classic advertising comparison of a product's effect.

clue.text: Many questions make this degree a poor one

definitions.text: Many questions make this degree a poor one

parts.words: Many questions make this degree a poor one
parts.note: a grilling by interrogators shares its ordinal with the lowest class of British honours degree

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase for harsh interrogation uses the same ordinal as the lowest grade of UK honours degree, regarded as a poor result.

clue.text: Work in factor for flight to Gretna?

indicators.note: in puts the short word for work inside the word for factor

parts.note: a factor or component is an element
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Somebody is putting effort into a key consideration for a trip north.
explanation.walkthrough: Gretna Green, just over the Scottish border, was where English couples ran away to marry; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Running off to marry in secret is an elopement, and Gretna Green was the classic destination.

clue.text: Composer ignores a Green artist

indicators.note: ignores tells us to drop the letter a from the composer's name

parts.note: Edward Elgar was an English composer
eco- describes green, environmentally friendly things

explanation.surface: A composer snubs an environmentalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignores a' removes one A from ELGAR, leaving ELGR.
explanation.definitionFit: El Greco was a Cretan-born painter working in Spain, so an artist.

clue.text: Crew cut back with extravagance in panic?

indicators.note: in puts the turned-round letters inside the word for panic

parts.note: a flap is a state of panic

indicators.note: back says the abbreviation for extravagance is read in reverse

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means extravagant excess

explanation.surface: A ship's company retreats extravagantly in alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns OTT into TTO, which goes into FLAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-top is a short haircut cropped level on top, a style of crew cut.

clue.text: Revolutionary air à la 'Les Mis' embraced by the French

definitions.text: Revolutionary air à la 'Les Mis' embraced by the French

indicators.note: embraced by puts the shuffled letters between the letters of the French article

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: revolutionary signals the following letters turned around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, letters ALA
the musical's nickname, taken as written

explanation.surface: A rousing tune in the manner of the hit musical, adopted by the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' rearranges AIR + ALA + LESMIS into AMARSEILLAIS, which LE 'embraces'. The whole clue also describes the anthem, born in the French Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: The national anthem of France is a revolutionary song that a French crowd would sing.

clue.text: Be suspicious when alarm's let off

indicators.note: off, as in gone off or set off, signals the letters are disturbed

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Grow wary when the alarm goes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let off' looks like setting off the alarm, but 'let' is fodder and 'off' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To smell a rat is an idiom meaning to suspect that something is wrong.

clue.text: Perhaps grandfather clock that's antique

definitions.meaning: an elderly person, such as a grandfather, is a veteran
an old clock is literally an aged timepiece

explanation.definitionFit: An old-timer is a veteran or elderly person, and read literally it is an aged timepiece like an antique clock.

clue.text: Old Mayor in revelling helped enjoy folk song

indicators.note: in places the mayor's name inside the jumbled letters
revelling suggests riotous disorder, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: Ken Livingstone was formerly Mayor of London

explanation.surface: A former mayor, out partying, helped people enjoy a traditional tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revelling' is the anagram signal, and 'Old Mayor' is Ken Livingstone, the first Mayor of London, whose name goes into the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: D'ye Ken John Peel is a traditional English hunting song from Cumbria.

clue.text: Place to do porridge, put another way, the nick

indicators.note: put another way says the letters of the next words are rearranged

explanation.surface: The prison, said differently, is where you do your time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do porridge' and 'nick' are British slang for serving time and prison, but the definition reads literally: where you cook oats.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen is where you make porridge, the oat breakfast.

clue.text: Two separate articles penned by Bloom — rising author

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, in reverse
penned by puts an article inside the flower
separate means the two articles go in at different places

parts.note: a lupin is a flowering plant, a bloom
a is the indefinite article
the second of the two articles, also a

explanation.surface: Two articles written by Bloom are on the rise.
explanation.walkthrough: Two A's go separately into LUPIN, giving LUAPIAN, which 'rising' turns upward. Bloom looks like Leopold Bloom of Ulysses, but it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: V. S. Naipaul was a Nobel-winning Trinidad-born British novelist.

clue.text: One will rub out monarch after long periods

indicators.note: after places the monarch's letters following the periods

parts.note: eras are long periods of time
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A ruler will wipe out rivals after ages.
explanation.definitionFit: An eraser is a rubber, something that will rub out marks.

clue.text: Famous stone arranged in round

indicators.note: in puts arranged's synonym inside round's

parts.note: a rota is a round or rotation of duties
set means arranged, placed in order

explanation.surface: A celebrated rock has been arranged in a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rosetta Stone is the famous inscribed slab that unlocked Egyptian hieroglyphs.

clue.text: Stick the workforce

definitions.meaning: the employees of an organisation collectively

explanation.definitionFit: A staff is a long stick, and staff are the people employed, the workforce.

clue.text: Pan requiring expertise and used by Michel Roux

parts.note: skill means expertise
the chef is French, and et is French for and

explanation.surface: A cooking pan calls for talent and is used by a celebrated French chef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and used by Michel Roux' asks for the French word for 'and', since Roux is a French chef.
explanation.definitionFit: A skillet is a frying pan, especially a heavy cast-iron one.

clue.text: Eat this cooked with toppings of grated Parmesan

definitions.text: Eat this cooked with toppings of grated Parmesan

indicators.note: cooked suggests ingredients prepared and mixed, so the letters are reshuffled
toppings of picks the first letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: An instruction to eat a pasta dish with grated cheese on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' mixes EAT THIS with G and P, the tops of 'grated' and 'Parmesan'; the whole clue also describes the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Long pasta strands are commonly eaten cooked with grated Parmesan on top.

clue.text: Intend to carry Britain right to the top

indicators.note: to carry means the word for intend holds the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: to aim is to intend

explanation.surface: A plan to hoist Britain to the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something filled to the brim is full right up to the top.

clue.text: Screen in the middle best clothes industrial plant

indicators.note: in the middle picks the central pair of letters of the word screen

parts.note: finery is one's best clothes

explanation.surface: A screen shows people in their best clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A refinery is a factory where crude oil or sugar is purified, an industrial plant.

clue.text: Lousy racehorse left in care of old man

indicators.note: in care of puts the letter for left inside, held by the old man

parts.note: pater is a dated word for father, the old man

explanation.surface: A poor horse is left in the care of an elderly man.
explanation.definitionFit: A plater is a mediocre racehorse that runs in minor races for a plate prize.
